result.title: Sharp Bounds on the Winner's Bias under Independent and Nonnegatively Correlated Noise
result.summary: Reporting the best of $M$ noisy, unbiased scores overstates the winner's value by up to $c\sqrt{V}$, where $V$ is the total noise variance and the sharp constant $c$ depends on how the noise is dependent. It was known only at the two extremes, arbitrary dependence ($\sqrt{(M-1)/M}$) and i.i.d. noise. We determine it for two classes in between: for independent, not identically distributed noise it is $\sqrt{(M-1)/(2M)}$, and for pairwise nonnegatively correlated noise it is $(M-1)/M$; for uncorrelated noise this answers the maximum version of an open question about the expected range. Explicit finite constructions attain both. As a corollary, the bias of the cross-validation estimator is bounded sharply within each class. All theorems are formally verified in Lean 4. Across 448 language-model and classifier selection pipelines, designs with per-candidate items realize a median 0.75 of the independent-class ceiling. At a fixed item budget, scoring all candidates on shared items is markedly less optimistic than giving each candidate its own items.

AI.brief_summary: 该文确定「胜者偏差」（M 个含噪无偏分数取最大导致的高估）在独立非同分布与非负相关噪声两类情形下的尖锐常数，用 Lean 4 形式化验证，并在 448 个语言模型与分类器选择流程上测量实际偏差。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 best-of-N、验证器筛选候选等推理侧评价相关：从多条候选轨迹或答案中取最优会系统性高估收益，且噪声相关结构（共享题项 vs 各自题项）可能影响候选评分设计与增益报告，可供核查。
